title: They Called Themselves Romans
sentences: The Byzantines never called themselves Byzantines.
They called themselves Romaioi, which means Romans.
Their state was the empire of the Romans, ruled from Constantinople.
Byzantine comes from Byzantium, the city's old Greek name.
A German scholar, Hieronymus Wolf, helped make the label popular in 1557.
Even their Ottoman conquerors called them Rum, meaning Romans.
Follow for more from the fall of Constantinople.
caption:
The Byzantines never called themselves Byzantines. They called themselves Romans.
